title: First Year Seminar - Leadership Emphasis
description: Provides opportunities for students to interact with faculty and staff in a small seminar setting. Students develop learning strategies, time management, and interpersonal skills, and are introduced to various campus resources (e.g., library, advising, career, health and wellness services, etc.)

title: Exploring Leadership
description: Understanding, applying and critiquing leadership theories, examining personal strengths, values, goals, and philosophy of leadership.
notes: Not open to students with credit in ARP 205.

title: Leadership - Campus Leadership Experience
description: Laboratory on campus and at other postsecondary settings to integrate academic work with experiences on campus and in postsecondary settings.
notes: Not open to students with credit in ARP 250 or ARP 403

title: Leadership Community Service
description: Community service and concepts associated with the servant leadership model.
notes: Not open to students with credit in EDL 206. Not open to students with six units of credit in ARP 207 or ARP 307.

title: Introduction to Leadership Inquiry
description: Introduction to qualitative and quantitative methods used to investigate leadership. Strategies to become critical and well-informed consumers of published research. Concepts and applications of analytical, empirical, and qualitative research methods. Access, examine, and critique leadership research.

title: Leadership Development
description: Leadership development strategies in community, professional, and non-profit sectors. Action-based learning. Choices and actions for self, teams, organizations, and communities. Equity-driven coaching, facilitation, and training strategies. Build leadership competence through applied research, collaboration, and reflection.

title: Self-Leadership: Internship and Career Readiness
description: Internship. Hours to be arranged. Career readiness best practices to include interviewing strategies, job search strategies, resume development, social capital, and networking.
notes: Not open to students with credit in ARP 404 or EDL 404

title: Enacting Leadership
description: Advanced leadership theories applied to real-world practice. Ethical leadership, self-awareness, and team collaboration. Effective communication and organizational strategies for leading in diverse and dynamic professional environments. Engage in the industry challenge.
notes: Not open to students with credit in ARP 405 and EDL 405

title: Ethnography of Organizational Culture and Leadership
description: Conduct independent research utilizing ethnography, qualitative research methods, and personal narrative. Observing naturally occurring interactions drawn from a variety of leadership and organizational settings. Primary methods of gathering data include: participant observation, interviewing, appreciative inquiry, critical perspectives, visual strategies, fieldnotes, and other approaches.

title: Organizational Assessment
description: Best practices, models, theories, tools for assessing organizational performance. Assessment as diagnostic intervention. Practical applications and frameworks for the collection, analysis, and interpretation/meaning of data to inform decision-making.

title: Special Study
notes: Not open to students with six units of credit in ARP 499.
